cards.text: Moses, the LORD's servant, has died. Now the LORD speaks to Joshua son of Nun, who was Moses' assistant. Friend, that's the assistant getting THE phone call: the boss is gone, and guess who's up.

cards.question: The LORD tells Joshua to get up, along with all the people, and cross over into the land. What do they have to cross?

cards.text: The LORD says He is giving that land to the children of Israel. GIVING, friend, not rent-to-own with a surprise payment at the end.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says this promise of land, every place where the sole of their foot will tread, is something brand new He never promised anyone before.

cards.text: Then the LORD lays out the borders: from the wilderness and Lebanon to the great River Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and west as far as the Great Sea. Friend, this is NOT a starter home.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD warns Joshua that a few enemies will still be able to stand against him.
The LORD tells Joshua He will be with him just as He was with ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD says, "I will never leave you nor forsake you." Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer wondering if anybody remembered me, so believe me, that line hits DIFFERENT.

cards.question: With a promise like that behind him, the LORD gives Joshua a command for the job ahead. What is it?
Why does Joshua need to be strong and courageous?

answers.text: He will give the people the land
He will build the LORD a temple
He will judge the people's disputes

cards.text: Then the LORD turns the volume UP: "Above all, be strong and very courageous." Not kinda brave on a good day, friend, VERY courageous.

cards.question: Being very courageous comes with a job. What does the LORD tell Joshua to be careful to observe?

answers.text: All the customs of the land
All the orders of the elders

cards.question: True or false: The LORD tells Joshua not to turn from the law to the right or to the left.

cards.text: Then the LORD says this Book of the Law must not depart from Joshua's mouth. Friend, that is NOT a book you read once and leave in the glove box with the car manual.

cards.question: How often does the LORD tell Joshua to meditate on the Book of the Law?
Joshua meditates on the Book of the Law so he will be careful to ___ everything written in it.

cards.text: Do all that, and the LORD says Joshua will prosper and succeed in all he does. Then He says it a third time, like a coach looking you dead in the eye: "Have I not commanded you to be strong and courageous?"

cards.question: The LORD tells Joshua not to be afraid and not to be discouraged. Why?

answers.text: The LORD is with him wherever he goes
The enemy armies have already fled
The people will fight every battle for him

cards.text: Then Joshua commands the officers of the people. Friend, the man got the job and went STRAIGHT to the group chat.

cards.question: Joshua's officers go through the camp with his message. What do they tell the people to prepare?
Joshua's message says that within ___ days the people will cross the Jordan to take possession of the land.

cards.text: But Joshua has a separate word for the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh. He tells them to remember what Moses, the servant of the LORD, commanded them.

cards.question: Moses told these tribes the LORD would give them their land. What else did he say the LORD would give them?

cards.text: These tribes already have land, because Moses gave it to them on this side of the Jordan. Their house is DONE, friend, while everybody else is still house hunting.

cards.question: True or false: Joshua says the wives, young children and livestock of these tribes may stay in the land Moses gave them.
But the mighty men of valor from these tribes get a different job. What is it?

answers.text: Cross over armed ahead of their brothers
Stay behind and guard their families
Go back and guard the land of Moab

cards.question: True or false: Joshua says these fighting men can go home as soon as everyone has crossed the Jordan.

cards.text: Once the LORD gives their brothers rest and their brothers possess their land, then they can go back to their own land on the east side of the Jordan. Friend, that's family: your own move is done, and you STILL show up to carry your brother's couch.

cards.question: Then Joshua gets his answer. What do they promise him?

answers.text: To think it over for a while
To wait for a sign from heaven

cards.question: Then they bless Joshua: "And may the LORD your God be with you, as He was with ___."

cards.text: They also promise to obey Joshua just as they obeyed Moses, and that blessing sounds familiar. The LORD promised Joshua the same thing at the start, and now he's hearing it from them too.

cards.question: Then they get serious. What do they say should happen to anyone who rebels against Joshua's orders?

answers.text: They will be put to death
They will be sent out of camp
They will pay a heavy fine

cards.question: True or false: They finish by telling Joshua, "Above all, be strong and courageous!"

cards.text: The LORD said it, and now they're saying it too, so Joshua is hearing this one in SURROUND SOUND. And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because this story is just getting started.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 12 quotes "And may the LORD your God be with you, as He was with ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Be quiet and careful" is half true in this passage. In Joshua 1:7 the LORD tells Joshua, "Be careful to observe all the law." A baker could argue that "careful" is something the LORD commands here.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: "Being very courageous comes with a job" ties courage and keeping the law together as one assignment. Joshua 1:7 gives them as two commands side by side and doesn't say how they connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh appear here for the first time, and nothing says who they are, for example that they are tribes of Israel.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question "What do they promise him?" never says who "they" are, and cards 14 and 15 also rely on an unnamed "they." The choice-card rule asks for that context. But Joshua 1:16 only says "they answered Joshua," so it leaves open whether the speakers are the two and a half eastern tribes or all the people. Filling in either one would break the leave-open rule.
findings.question: When a choice card has to say who is speaking, but the text leaves the speaker open (Joshua 1:16), should the card name the group the context suggests (the Reubenites, Gadites and half-tribe of Manasseh)? Or should it use a neutral phrase like "the people answering Joshua," or something else?

findings.problem: "Then they bless Joshua" calls their words a blessing. Joshua 1:17 doesn't call them that. They say, "May the LORD your God be with you," which is the same situation as the Naomi example in the rule.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)

findings.problem: "That blessing sounds familiar" also calls the words of Joshua 1:17 a blessing, which the text doesn't do.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them. ❌ "Naomi asks the LORD to bless them." ✅ "Naomi tells them, 'May the LORD…'" (Ruth 1:8)

findings.problem: This card asks about "be strong and courageous" again, in Joshua 1:18. The line repeats through the passage (1:6, 1:7, 1:9, 1:18), and stop 1 card 9 already asked about it the first time it appeared.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.
